This site's Far View and Badger House complexes preserve remnants of an earlier Basketmaker Culture. A 4-story square tower is located off Navajo Canyon close to a ceremonial structure known as the Sun Temple at this location, and several features including T-shaped windows and spiral petroglyphs may link it to the Chaco Canyon culture. The Wetherill family is credited with the discovery of this location, which contains a structure with over 150 rooms, including 23 ► kivas. The Spruce Tree House was the last major structure built at this location before it was abandoned around 1275. Identify this site in southwestern Colorado, a national park that contains the largest cliff dwellings of the Ancestral Puebloans.

The Ten Saints are a mountain range on this island, which also contains a monument to Sir Thomas Maitland and a bridge named after Kaiser Wilhelm II. The relics of its patron, Saint Spyridon, are thought to have saved this island from an 18th-century Ottoman invasion. The murder of Enrico Tellini, which was blamed on Albanian bandits, set off a 1923 international incident named after this island. It is part of a chain that also includes Lefkas, Paxos, Zante, and ► Kephalonia. Name this northernmost of Greece's Ionian Islands.

Three species of Rhododendron are known as the tea of this region, whose Smallwood Reservoir was blamed for flooding hunting lands of the Innu people. Smaller cities in this region include Red Bay, Cartwright, and the site of a Moravian mission, Hopedale. The city named after this region, a center of iron ore mining, is across a provincial boundary from Wabush. This region may take its name from an early modern Portuguese term for a ► landholder, such as Joao Fernandes, one of its early explorers. Quebec's northeastern border is with what Canadian region, the mainland portion of a province shared with Newfoundland?

A Polish expedition to this region's Nemegt Formation uncovered a skeleton of Tarbosaurus, a tyrannosaur-like predator. Another expedition here used a convoy of Dodge cars to discover eggs that were once thought to be from Protoceratops but have since been discovered to belong to Oviraptor. That expedition was led by Roy Chapman Andrews. The southwestern portion of this region is the Alashan Plateau, which was thought to have been an inland sea by the Russian geographer Nikolai Przhevalsky, who gave his name to the wild horse that once lived here. The Gashun region of this desert is still home to some ► Bactrian camels. The Dorno- and Dund- aimags, or provinces of Mongolia, take their name from, what cold desert of north-central Asia?

A large collection of stones arranged in a wheel-shaped circle is located atop Medicine Mountain in this state, which is also the location of the headwaters of the Belle Fourche River, which flows by the bright-red Spearfish Formation. It contains a number of plant fossils from the Eocene Epoch at Fossil Butte and its highest point is considered second only to Mt. McKinley in difficulty and contains a namesake glacier, the largest in the Rockies. In addition to Gannett Peak, which is also the highest in the Wind River Range, this state contains Independence Rock as well as a passage between the Sweetwater and Green Rivers that crosses not only an endorheic basin within the Great Divide but ► South Pass as well. Also containing the Paint Pots and Grand Prismatic Spring, identify this state that contains Grand Teton and Yellowstone.

The Ai-Petri mountain in this region contains the headwaters for the Uchan-Su River, which passes over a notable waterfall, and the Kerchenska Gulf on its East separates this region from the mud volcanoes of the Taman Peninsula. The Baydar Gate is a mountain pass in this area and the Sarych Cape contains a controversially foreign-staffed lighthouse in this region, which contains a number of mountainous plateaus known as Yaylas including the highest in the region of Babugan. The ancient Greek settlement of Chersonesos Tauria is located in this region, and it contains a walking trail called the "Tsar's Path" which passes by sights like the Swallow's Nest. ► Simferopol is the capital of, what autonomous province that also features the town of Inkerman and the port of Sevastopol?

The Chavacano creole is spoken in parts of this island, which along with Dinagat is one of two islands inhabited by members of genus Podogymnura, the so-called "moon rats." Threatened forests on this island are sometimes run by PICOP and can be found on Mount Kitanglad and around the Bukidnon Plateau. The Zamboanga Peninsula is the western end of this island inhabited by so-called "Moros," whose chief city is ► Davao. The Abu Sayyaf insurgency operates on what southernmost major island of the Philippines?

This state's city of Calvillo is a major center of the guava industry. Other sights here include the Cerro del Muerto and the ghost towns in its northern region of Tepezala. The San Marcos Fair takes place in this state, which is the site of a museum devoted to the broadsheets produced by Jose Guadalupe Posada. Its capital, which shares the same name as the state, was the location of a 1914 convention called by Venustiano Carranza but soon taken over by Villistas. It is located between Zacatecas, from which it separated in 1857, and Jalisco. For 15 points, name this third-smallest Mexican state whose name is Spanish for "hot waters."

One island in this group has a silhouette consisting of three basaltic columns. Prospective visitors may reach it by passing the Utter Maurby breakwater, but are to be given "detailed vomiting instructions" beforehand. The inhabitants of the Innner island of this name "practically laid out the welcome mat for the Romans" and were transported en masse to Australia, where they became an important immigrant community in Brisbane. Their home was "barely even an island," being connected to the mainland by a tidal sandbar. Another native of this region who was saved from marauding janissaries is ► Eliza, who appears in The Baroque Cycle. Name this difficult-to-pronounce analogue of the Hebrides found in Neal Stephenson's Cryptonomicon.

The mythology of these people includes spirits called kelets, including herds of deer with obsidian hooves and an eight-pawed polar bear. Their kinship structures were studied by an exiled Polish anthroplogist, Waldemar Bogoraz. In the 1730s a military expedition sent to conquer these people was led by a man about whom it was said that "wolverines fall dead from his breath." That man, Dmitri Pavlutsky, was captured and roasted alive by these people, who also drove off their traditional rivals the Yukaghirs and the Koryaks. Most people of this ethnicity live on a peninsula whose chief city is Anadyr; their language is thought to be related to that spoken on ► Kamchatka. The name of what Paleo-Siberian people also applies to the sea located just north of the Bering Strait?

This island group was home to Microgoura meeki, an extinct species of crested pigeon that lived on an island named for Louis XV's foreign minister. A second island in this group was the site of an aborted Spanish colony that resulted in the deaths of both native leader Malope and Alvaro de Mendana, who gave this island group its name. This group's capital is built around the Kukum Highway at the mouth of the Matanikau River east of Point Cruz, which was the site of an ►amphibious invasion led by Alexander Vandegrift also called Operation Watchtower. Choiseul, Nendo, and Guadalcanal are all found in what Pacific nation whose capital is Honiara?

Aime Cesaire wrote a poem describing the "roar of silence and night" he heard while listening to this mountain. Its southwestern slope contains a series of cones called the Rushayo chain, which produce melilitite that is rich in olivine; most of the main peak's lavas are feldspathoidal. An ERS tandem mission was used to map an eruption of this volcano in response to a request from the Belgian Civil Protection Agency. Shaheru and Baruta are craters on the side of this stratovolcano, which is found south of Nyamulagira in the Virunga Mountains. A noted lava lake is found in the central crater of, for 15 points, what volcano that overlooks the Congolese city of Goma on Lake Kivu?

A memorial designed by Ron Magers and Shelly Bradbury attempts to replicate this feature, which was stabilized with four turnbuckles after quarryman E. H. Geddes used cement to prevent water from leaking into it. The construction of Interstate 93 produced an Environmental Impact Statement about the preservation of this feature, which survived the blasting process under the care of the Nielsen family. It rose on the side of Cannon Mountain above Profile Lake before it collapsed on the night of May 3, 2003. Nathaniel Hawthorne called it "a work of nature in her mood of majestic playfulness" in his story "The Great ► Stone Face." what ex-feature of Franconia Notch State Park appears next to the slogan "Live Free or Die" on the New Hampshire state quarter?

The only species in genus Rhodostethia is a gull named for this man, notable for its black necklace and pink chest; that species was found nesting at Churchill, Manitoba in 1980. The strait between King William Land and the Boothia Peninsula is named for this man, who was frozen in there on an expedition with his uncle John and captained HMS Cove on a voyage that failed to save the stranded whaling ship William Torr. He remarked that "there's no more chance of sailing through that than through the cliffs of Dover" when he discovered a feature he called the Victoria Barrier. Although he's not John Franklin, he led the Erebus and Terror on an 1841 expedition that searched for the ► South Magnetic Pole. What British explorer's name is applied to Antarctica's largest ice shelf?

This was the site where the camp of the Sleepy Lizard Women was burned during a battle between the Liru and the Kuniya, a woma python whose mark can still be seen on this feature's surface. Notable deaths at this feature include those of gold prospector Harold Lasseter, who died of thirst looking for a reef near here in 1931, and infant Azaria Chamberlain, who disappeared here in 1980. This landmark is paired with Kata Tjuta, or Mount Olga, in the name of a national park. The Pitjantjatjara people, who hold this feature sacred, call it ► Uluru. Name this inselberg southwest of Alice Springs in the Northern Territory, a red sandstone monolith of the Australian Outback.

One of these entities named for the Lignumvitae tree is a botanical refuge near the village of Islamorada. One with "No Name" near Big Pine is home to a dwarf subspecies of white-tailed deer. Henry Flagler's Overseas Railroad connected these islands to the mainland until they were devastated by the Labor Day hurricane of 1935. The southernmost of these islands tried to proclaim independence as the ► "Conch Republic" and was the setting for To Have and Have Not, a novel by local resident Ernest Hemingway. The populated part of Monroe County, Florida is what chain of islands, examples of which include "Largo" and "West"?

Although this park isn't in the state of Michigan, it contains a Saginaw Bay, and its more interestingly-named locations include Cranberry Bay. Koochiching State Forest lies to the west of this park. A gold rush to this park's Little American Island began in 1893. Popular sites to visit in this park include the Ellsworth Rock Gardens and Kettle Falls, which includes a dam built in 1910 as well as a hotel built by Ed Rose. Located near International Falls, this park features locations such as Kabetogama Lake and Rainy Lake. Exploring this park requires plenty of water travel; its name comes from a group of ► fur traders who traded with the Ojibwe around the US-Canadian border. Name this national park in northeast Minnesota.

The Nilgiri Hills are in the western part of this state near its second-largest city of Coimbatore, and the Pallavi Kingdom was centered in this present-day state at Kanchipuram, one of the holiest cities in Hinduism. This state is home to the delta of the Kaveri River, which flows into the state from Karnataka. This state, which borders on the Gulf of Mannar and has the northern terminus of Adam's Bridge, surrounds the city of Pondicherry. Lying east of Kerala and south of Andhra Pradesh, this state was formerly known as Madras State, and members of this state's namesake ethnic group tried to create a breakaway republic in nearby Sri Lanka. For 15 points, name this state of southern India with capital at Chennai.

One island on this body of water is home to three villages Â– Tooni, Saare, and Piiri. The last of those villages is home to a church of Old Believers, founded by the first inhabitants of that island of Piirissaar. Towns on the banks of this body of water include Gdov and Mustvee, and one city on its banks is home to the Mirozhsky Monastery, Pskov. The Velikaya River flows into this lake, and it is drained by the Narva. One part of this lake is called ► LÃ¤mmijÃ¤rv, and another is known as Pihkva. The largest trans-boundary lake in Europe is, what lake on the border of Estonia and Russia, the site of the 1242 Battle of the Ice?

The first Europeans in this region believed it to be inhabited by female warriors ruled by Queen Calafia. Early peoples here included the Cochimi, and the Pericu lived south of here. This polity contains the cities of Rosarito and Colonia Vicente Guerrero. The largest island in this modern day polity is separated from the mainland by the Ballenas fault, and is the uninhabited island of Isla Ãngel de la Guarda. This region contains the Sierra del JuÃ¡rez, and some of its larger cities are ► Ensenada and Mexicali. Dominated by the Vizcaino desert, this is, what Mexican state whose largest city is Tijuana, located on a peninsula south of California?

In December 2000 this country received UN aid after a blizzard that killed 16,000 livestock. Towns in this country include Suugant and Baruunturuun. An endangered species of wild horse that once lived in this country is named for Nikolai Przewalski. This country's largest lake is the Uvs Nuur, and its lowest altitude is at Hoh Nuur. This country is also home to the ► Khentii and AltaÃ¯ Mountains, along with the Selenge River, which flows from the KhangaÃ¯ mountains. Home to Lake Khovsgol, this is, what nation whose capital is at Ulaan Baatar, home to the northern part of the Gobi Desert, located south of Russia and north of China?

Though it is not Spain, this place is home to mountains named Valterne, Tortelosa, and Gayne. While it was forming, aluminum-26 and iron-60 provided a large amount of heat, making its interior warm and squishy, causing it to spin rapidly. This moon is home to an equatorial ridge of mountains that go nearly around the moon, and its craters, including Clarin, Almeric, Bramimond, and Charlemagne, as well as its Roncevaux Terra, derive their names from the Song of Roland. For 15 points, identify this walnut-shaped and distinctly two-toned moon discovered by Cassini, the ► third largest surrounding Saturn.

A literary description of this route calls it "such a river of life as nowhere else exists in the world" where "all the world [is] going and coming." Part of this route makes up the northeast segment of the ambitious Golden Quadrilateral highway construction project. The title Irish-born character and his lama traverse this route in a noted vignette in chapter 4 of Kipling's Kim. It crosses the Khyber Pass on its way out of Pakistan. For 15 points, name this road that links Chittagong, Bangladesh to Kabul, Afghanistan, which passes through Delhi, Islamabad, and most of northern India

The Knights of the Golden Horseshoe Expedition led some of the first non-natives into this geographic region after crossing the Swift Run Gap. The Three Notch'd Road crosses into this valley at Jarmans Gap and was a major thoroughfare for settlers entering this region in the 18th century. A major figure in this valley's development was Claudius Crozet, who helped survey and construct railroad tunnels through the ► Blue Ridge and co-founded a "military institute" located in this valley. Victories at Port Republic and Front Royal were won by Stonewall Jackson during an 1862 campaign for control of, what Virginia valley?

The first capital of this historical polity was named after Otto Finsch, who first negotiated for this polity to become a colony of its parent country. Finsch, along with banker Adolph von Hansemann, founded an eponymously named company to aid the colonization of it in 1884. A treaty in 1899 allowed this polity's parent country to incorporate islands to this polity's north, such as the Caroline and Mariana Islands. In 1914, this polity was occupied by Australia, which caused Hermann Detzner to flee inland and write Four Years among the Cannibals, which details adventures climbing the Kratke Range and crossing the Sepik River. For 20 points, name this Pacific colony which was once named for Kaiser Wilhelm and later acquired the name "Papua."

North of this city is the Kamfers Dam which provides water to this city, and is a major breeding ground of lesser flamingos. Griquas, a rugby union squad from this city, plays its home games at GWK Park and has won the Currie Cup three times. The settlement of this city was sparked when Erasmus Jacobs found a 21.25 carat gemstone near this city in 1866. A 240 meter deep, 460 meter wide mine is this city's "Big Hole," where an 80-carat ► diamond was later found. That hole was a large diamond mine which was owned and operated by the De Beers company, which was founded by Cecil Rhodes. Name this South African city, the capital of the Northern Cape Province.

In 1994, Ruth Shady Solis began excavating in this country's Norte Chico region, at a site known as Caral, which was dated to be founded before 2600 BCE. Further north, along the Fortaleza River, is the even older site of Huaricanga, which is dated to 3500 BCE. In the southern part of this country, in the Osmore River Valley, is Cerro Baul, a large mesa which was the meeting point for two ancient cultures who both worshiped the "Staff God," the Wari and the Tiwanaku. Also in this country was the Chimor culture, whose capital was at Chan Chan. ► name this country which is better known for sites of the Inkan civilization such as Machu Picchu and Nazca

The west of this island contains a structure of karst limestone divided by cracks called "grikes"; Edmund Ludlow wrote that it was "a country where there is not enough water to drown a man, wood enough to hang one, nor earth enough to bury him." That region is called the "Burren," or "great rock" in the original language of this island, which was also used to write the Annals of the Four Masters. Medieval structures on this island included artificial islands called crannogs and ringforts called raths. A rebellion on this island tried to take over the ► Four Courts, Phoenix Park, and the General Post Office in 1916. The Easter Rising took place on what "Emerald Isle" whose cities include Cork, Limerick, and Dublin?

A mob war for control of this city's dry cleaning business involved the "Woodland Mob" led by Maxie Diamond and led to the rise of Shondor Birns, named "Public Enemy #1" by this city's newspapers. Ahmed Evans, the leader of this city's "Afro Set" black nationalists, was accused of helping start the Hough Riots that broke out in this city in 1966. This city's Euclid Avenue, known as "Millionaire's Row," was where a monument was built to Mark Hanna. This city was founded on land claimed by Connecticut, the so-called "Western ► Reserve" territory. The Horseshoe Casino was recently opened in this city by Dan Gilbert, the owner of its NBA franchise. In 1969 the Cuyahoga River caught fire in what northeast Ohio city on Lake Erie?

The town of El BÃºfalo lies in this state, along with SatevÃ³ and Urique. The Recohuata Hot Springs are located in this state, along with Lake Arareco and the Samalayuca Dunes. Near Janos in this state, archeological digs occur at PaquimÃ©. This state's town of Creel, a stop on the "El Chepe" train, lies roughly 50 miles from Basaseachic Falls. At Ojinaga in this state, the RÃ-o Conchos ends, and it is home to the cities of Delicias and Parral. Deeper in parts than Arizona's Grand Canyon, Copper Canyon lies in its southwest. Its capital shares its name, while its largest city, across the ► Rio Grande from El Paso, is Ciudad JuÃ¡rez. Name this state bordering New Mexico, Sonora, and Texas, the largest in Mexico, which lends its name to a breed of small dogs.
Free and Sovereign State of Chihuahua

It is not the Matterhorn, but the Pogyos route to the top of this mountain was used for its first ascent, by Edward Whymper in 1880. From the 16th to the early 19th centuries, it was assumed to be the tallest mountain in the world, though it is not even in the top 100. Nearby residents refer to this mountain as the "Mountain of Ice." A poem inspired by it, "Mi Delirio sobre [this mountain]," was written by Simon Bolivar. A namesake battle in the valley near this mountain saw Sebastian de Belalcazar's forces attack those of Ruminahui. On a clear day, this peak in the Cordillera Occidental can be seen 90 miles away in ► Guayaquil. Name this inactive stratovolcano, the farthest point on the Earth's surface from its center, the tallest mountain in the Ecuadorean Andes.

The endangered and venomous Latifi's Viper is endemic to this nation. Islands off the coast of this country include Ashooradeh, Hendurabi, and Sirri, and its Urmia Lake has 102 islands. The Karun and Karkheh rivers flow through its lowland region of Khuzestan. This nation's fourth-largest city contains the tomb of the poet Kamal Khujandi and the ruins of an Ikhanid-period mosque known as the "ark"; that city is ► Tabriz. The highest point in this country, Mount Damavand, is located in its Alborz Mountains. Its southern border terminates at the Arvand Rud, which a nation to its west calls the Shatt Al-Arab. What country that borders both the Gulf of Oman and the Caspian Sea fought a war in the 1980s with its western neighbor, Iraq?

Most communications to and from this island are handled by the antenna farm on Pillar Mountain. This island's Historical Society is located in the Baranov Museum, named for the man who relocated the main settlement here from Three Saints Bay in 1791. The Good Friday earthquake of 1964 led to a tsunami that destroyed two of this island's three salmon canneries. Fort Abercrombie is part of the Integrated Support Command maintained by the U.S. Coast Guard on this island, which lies across the Shelikof Strait from Katmai National Park. The U. A. Middendorffi subspecies of the ► grizzly bear is named for this island. Name this second-largest island in the U.S., located off the southern coast of Alaska.

Islands located in this body of water include Hogan Island, Three Hummock Island, and Curtis Island. Two oil and gas fields located in this body of water, Otway Basin and Gippsland Basin, send product to processing facilities in Altona and Geelong. The largest ports to the south of this body of water are Devonport, Ulverstone, and Penguin, while to its north is Wilsons Promontory National Park, home to its country's southernmost mainland lighthouse. Its so-called namesake "triangle" has been compared to the "Bermuda" one, prompting construction of a lighthouse on Deal Island in 1848. The largest islands in this body of water are King Island, once home to dwarf black ► emus, and the Furneaux Group which includes Clark, Cape Barren, and Flinders Island. Name this strait, south of the state of Victoria, which separates Tasmania from Australia.

The 1971 Erkweit Conference held in this city made plans to establish its university. A recently completed railroad connects it to Lanya in the south and Mangall in the north. This city's biggest commercial center is known as Malakia. Two of this city's most notable attractions are the rocky hill of Jebel Kujur and the mausoleum of John Garang, a Dinka rebel leader who died in a 2005 helicopter crash. Originally a trading post named Gongokoro, this city serves as the capital of Central Equatoria, the smallest of the ten states in its nation. The planned city of Ramciel will likely replace it as national capital, a status it has ► only held since July 2011. Name this city situated on the White Nile, the largest city and capital of South Sudan.

This region's ports include Lemonwood and Planky Town, both of which lie near the mouth of the Greenblood river. Grey Gallows island, which is part of the Stepstones archipelago, lies to the east of this region. The Red Mountains of this region can be crossed through the Prince's Pass, which contains the Tower of Joy, or through the Boneway Pass, which is overlooked by the fortress of Yronwood ["ironwood"] and which connects this region to the Stormlands. Many of this region's inhabitants are descended from Rhoynish invaders who intermarried with Andals, and this region maintains the Rhoynish custom of allowing female succession. The ► Water Gardens were constructed to please a princess of this region, which is governed from Sunspear by a family whose words are "Unbent, Unbowed, Unbroken." Doran Martell rules--for 10 points--what southern peninsula of Westeros in George R. R. Martin's A Song of Ice and Fire?

This region's Fort Selkirk was a trading post attacked by Chilkats. Nelruna is the native name for a young volcano in this location that has the creative name of Volcano Mountain. The Signpost Forest can be found in this region's town of Watson Lake. Ibex Valley is located in this territory, which is connected by the Dempster Highway to the city of Inuvik. ► Dawson City was a boomtown founded in this region, which is also the location of Mount Logan. This territory's population skyrocketed with the Klondike gold rush. Name this territory of Canada, which shares its name with a river that flows through its western neighbor Alaska, and has its capital at Whitehorse.

These were created by removing iron oxide pebbles to expose a wind-resistant layer of lime. One crackpot theory of these structures holds that they were gigantic looms used to create textile patterns like those of the nearby Paracas culture. German archaeologist Maria Reiche worked to preserve these features, which were endangered by the building of the Pan-American highway. Airplanes are the best way to view these features, a fact which has caused noted crank Erich von Daniken to postulate that they were actually the runways of ancient spacefaring aliens. A monkey with a spiral tail is one example of these, but of greater interest to this tournament's editor are the so-called "Pelican," "Heron," and "Condor." ► name this set of ancient glyphs that stretch for miles across arid regions of southern Peru.

The Russian oil tanker Volgoneft-248 broke in half during a storm in this body of water, causing a major 1999 oil spill. Another vessel that sank in this body of water was the Australian submarine AE2, which was scuttled near Kara Burnu Point. The Granicus River flows into this body of water, one of whose islands, Buyukkada, served for four years as a place of exile for Leon Trotsky. In ancient times, it was known as the Propontis; its present name derives from another island, which was used as a quarry for white ► marble. Water flows into this sea from the Bosporus and out through the Dardanelles into the Aegean. Name this inland sea in Turkey.

"The Boy who Waterskied to Forever" and "What Came Ashore at Lirios" are two of the "Tales of" this region in a short story collection by James Tiptree, Jr. This territory's town of Chan Santa Cruz, a center of resistance during the Caste War, was renamed to honor a man called the "red dragon with eyes of jade," Felipe Carillo Puerto. It was named for a patriot who assisted Jose Maria Morelos in drafting the Constitution of Apatzingan. Chetumal is the capital of this state, whose southern border adjoins Belize. In 1974, this territory became the 30th of Mexico's states. For 20 points, Cancun is located in what Caribbean coastal state of Mexico, south and east of the state of Yucatan?

Thomas Cole's painting View from Mount Holyoke, Northampton, Massachusetts, after a Thunderstorm is better known by the name of this kind of landform, which appears at right-center. One of these called "Reelfoot" was created in west Tennessee by the action of the New Madrid earthquake. One called "Providence" was the subject of a scheme by Ulysses S. Grant's engineers to bypass the fortress of Vicksburg. A "billabong" is the Australian term for this kind of landform, which appears in the title of a novel about a ► lynch mob by Walter Van Tilburg Clark. Identify this kind of lake, formed when a meander is cut off from the main course of a river.

This body of water is home to Fort Ives and its upper portion is known as the Bedford Basin. Its Narrows is crossed by the MacKay and Macdonald Bridges, connecting its namesake city to Dartmouth. This body of water is home to children's television character Theodore Tugboat and was the site of one of the collision of the SS Imo and the SS Mont-Blanc during World War I, which caused an explosion that killed nearly 2,000 people in what is believed to be the largest accidental explosion in history. ► name this Canadian harbor in Nova Scotia's largest city.

This body of water is jutted into by Cape Froward on the Brunswick Peninsula, which features a large metallic cross. Fuerta Bulnes was an establishment along this body of water, which connects to the Smyth Channel and is near the home of the Kaweskar people. A 16th-century attempt to settle near this body of water ended when all of the settlers either starved or froze to death; English captain Thomas Cavendish, who found the remains of the colony, called the site "Port Famine." The Magdalena Channel is at this strait's western entrance. This strait's ► namesake, who was killed on Cebu in the Philippines, did not know of the nearby Beagle Channel or Drake Passage. Name this Chilean waterway that connects the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.

A plateau east of this city was said to grow after dusk to deter night attacks from enemies, causing it to be known as the "mountain of the night." This city's Cathedral of Our Lady of Victories is located along its nation's first paved road, Kingsway. This city contains its nation's only ski resort, Afri-Ski, which is located in the Maluti Mountains, and it is connected to the town of Marseilles in a neighboring country by rail through its namesake "branch line." Mazenod is a town close to this city, which lies on the Caledon River. This city's main airport is named after its country's greatest king, ► Moshoeshoe I. Name this capital of Lesotho.

This place was the capital of the Yuuhzhan Vong Empire. The Undercity on this object includes the districts of Sah'c Town, The Works, CoCo Town, and the Factory District. This body is located at the intersection of the Perlemian Trade Route, Metellos Trade Route, and the Leisure Corridor. Zam Wesell attempted to assassinate a prominent politician before being killed at the Outlander Club in the Galactic City on this planet. A battle on the Invisible Hand above this planet led to ► Obi-Wan and Anakin freeing Chancellor Palpatine. Name this Star Wars planet with galactic coordinates (0,0,0) [read as: zero, zero, zero] that is home to the Senate Building and Jedi Temple.

The Italian battleships Vittorio Veneto and Littorio were interned in this body of water during World War II. Located north of this body of water are Lake Manzala and Lake Timsah. Fifteen ships known as the Yellow Fleet were trapped in this lake until 1975 as a result of a war that started eight years before. This hypersaline lake blocked the lessepsian migration of species for many decades, preventing the colonization of Red Sea flora and fauna in the Mediterranean. Franklin Roosevelt met with Saudi King Aziz aboard the USS Quincy in 1945 in this lake. For 15 points, name this lake located within the Suez Canal. Drinking from it is not recommended!

This city's landmark of Aggmeda Khyang is a Buddhist sanctuary built on a group of round wooden columns. Muhammad Yunus proposed this city as the site of a "deep-sea mega-port." Its local name is "Panowa," but its usual English name commemorates a British East India Company officer sent to deal with a refugee crisis on the Arakan border. Located 150 kilometers south of Chittagong and home to the world's longest natural sandy beach, this is, for 20 points, what fishing port in Bangladesh situated on the Bay of Bengal?

In 2011, the Women's World Chess Championship match between Hou Yifan and Koneru Humpy was held in this nation. The 1997 Operation Libelle in this nation was the first time that German soldiers fired in combat since World War II. That event was a result of a rebel takeover in this country after a failed series of Ponzi schemes resulted in the country descending into anarchy.
